steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than other colors in the visible spectrum, causing it to scatter far more readily in all directions as sunlight passes through the air. When you look at any part of the sky (away from the sun), your eyes receive this scattered blue light from countless directions, making the whole sky appear blue.
